title: Explicit quotient presentation of a module pushout
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $P,Q,Q'$ be $R$-modules, and let $a:P\to Q$ and $b:P\to Q'$ be $R$-linear maps. Put $D=Q'\oplus Q$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-sum-modules], $\delta(x)=(b(x),-a(x))$, and $E=D/\delta(P)$ [def-weil-pbc-quotient-module], with quotient $\pi:D\to E$ and maps $j(y)=\pi(y,0)$, $k(z)=\pi(0,z)$. Then $\pi$ is surjective, $\ker\pi=\operatorname{im}\delta$, and $jb=ka$. For every $R$-module $T$ and linear maps $u:Q'\to T$, $v:Q\to T$ with $ub=va$, there is a unique linear map $h:E\to T$ such that $hj=u$ and $hk=v$, and it satisfies $h(\pi(y,z))=u(y)+v(z)$. In particular $(E,k,j)$ is a pushout of $(a,b)$, the colimit of the finite span in $R$-modules [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. For every chosen pushout $(Q'',c:Q\to Q'',b':Q'\to Q'')$ of $(a,b)$, there is a unique linear isomorphism $e:E\xrightarrow{\sim}Q''$ with $ej=b'$ and $ek=c$.

source.place: Tag 0AUM, lemma-domination-universally-injective, proof first paragraph: quotient of the direct sum by the image of (g,-f), expanded into its universal property and exact sequence.

proof.text: By the componentwise operations of [def-weil-pbc-direct-sum-modules], $\delta(x+x_1)=\delta(x)+\delta(x_1)$ and $\delta(rx)=r\delta(x)$. Thus $N=\delta(P)$ is a submodule: it contains $0$, and sums and scalar multiples are images of the corresponding sums and scalar multiples in $P$. Applying [def-weil-pbc-quotient-module] to $D,N$ gives a linear surjection $\pi:D\to E$ and $\ker\pi=N=\operatorname{im}\delta$.

source.place: Tag 0AUM (lemma-domination-universally-injective), first proof paragraph: expansion of the quotient construction.

proof.text: The coordinate inclusions and $\pi$ are linear, so $j,k$ are linear. For $x\in P$, $j(b(x))-k(a(x))=\pi(b(x),-a(x))=\pi(\delta(x))=0$, since $\delta(x)\in N$. Consequently $jb=ka$. Also $(y,z)=(y,0)+(0,z)$ gives $\pi(y,z)=j(y)+k(z)$.

source.place: Tag 0AUM (lemma-domination-universally-injective), first proof paragraph: expansion of the quotient construction.

proof.text: Given $u,v$ as in the statement, set $w(y,z)=u(y)+v(z)$. The coordinatewise operations show that $w$ is linear, and $w(\delta(x))=u(b(x))-v(a(x))=0$. Hence $w(N)\subseteq\{0\}$. Apply clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-quotient-module-induced-map] with $M=D$, $N=\operatorname{im}\delta$, $M'=T$, $N'=\{0\}$ (and $M''=T$, $N''=\{0\}$ for its unused third module). This gives $\bar w:E\to T/\{0\}$ with $\bar w(\pi(y,z))=w(y,z)+\{0\}$. The map $\epsilon:T/\{0\}\to T$, $t+\{0\}\mapsto t$, is well defined because these cosets are singletons, and is linear by the quotient operations. Put $h=\epsilon\bar w$. Then $h(\pi(y,z))=u(y)+v(z)$.

source.place: Tag 0AUM (lemma-domination-universally-injective), first proof paragraph: expansion of the quotient construction.

proof.text: Setting $z=0$ and $y=0$ in the formula just obtained gives $hj=u$ and $hk=v$. If $h_1:E\to T$ is another linear map with these identities, then $h_1(\pi(y,z))=h_1(j(y)+k(z))=u(y)+v(z)=h(\pi(y,z))$. Surjectivity of $\pi$ implies $h_1=h$.

source.place: Tag 0AUM (lemma-domination-universally-injective), first proof paragraph: expansion of the quotient construction.

proof.text: The indexing category of the span has three objects $P,Q,Q'$ and two nonidentity arrows $a,b$, so it is small. A cocone with vertex $T$ is precisely a pair $v:Q\to T$, $u:Q'\to T$ with $va=ub$; its map from $P$ must be this common composite. Steps 2--4 say precisely that the cocone with vertex $E$ and legs $k,j$ has the existence and uniqueness property of [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. It is therefore the required pushout.

source.place: Tag 0AUM (lemma-domination-universally-injective), first proof paragraph: expansion of the quotient construction.

proof.text: For the chosen pushout, its legs satisfy $b' b=ca$, so step 3 gives $e:E\to Q''$ with $ej=b'$ and $ek=c$. Its pushout property gives $d:Q''\to E$ with $db'=j$ and $dc=k$. The maps $de$ and $1_E$ have the same composites with $j,k$, hence agree by step 4. Likewise $ed$ and $1_{Q''}$ have the same composites with $b',c$, hence agree by uniqueness for the chosen pushout. Thus $e$ is a linear isomorphism with inverse $d$; any other such isomorphism has the same underlying linear map by step 4.

lean.statement: theorem pushout_quotient_presentation {R : Type u} [CommRing R] {P Q Q' : Type v} [AddCommGroup P] [AddCommGroup Q] [AddCommGroup Q'] [Module R P] [Module R Q] [Module R Q'] (a : P →ₗ[R] Q) (b : P →ₗ[R] Q') : Function.Surjective (pushoutQuotientMap a b) ∧ LinearMap.ker (pushoutQuotientMap a b) = LinearMap.range (pushoutRelation a b) ∧ (pushoutQuotientInl a b).comp b = (pushoutQuotientInr a b).comp a ∧ (∀ (T : Type t) [AddCommGroup T] [Module R T] (u : Q' →ₗ[R] T) (v : Q →ₗ[R] T), u.comp b = v.comp a → ∃ h : PushoutQuotient a b →ₗ[R] T, h.comp (pushoutQuotientInl a b) = u ∧ h.comp (pushoutQuotientInr a b) = v ∧ (∀ h' : PushoutQuotient a b →ₗ[R] T, h'.comp (pushoutQuotientInl a b) = u → h'.comp (pushoutQuotientInr a b) = v → h' = h) ∧ ∀ (y : Q') (z : Q), h (pushoutQuotientMap a b (y, z)) = u y + v z) ∧ CategoryTheory.IsPushout (ModuleCat.ofHom a) (ModuleCat.ofHom b) (ModuleCat.ofHom (pushoutQuotientInr a b)) (ModuleCat.ofHom (pushoutQuotientInl a b)) ∧ (∀ (Q'' : Type v) [AddCommGroup Q''] [Module R Q''] (c : Q →ₗ[R] Q'') (b' : Q' →ₗ[R] Q''), CategoryTheory.IsPushout (ModuleCat.ofHom a) (ModuleCat.ofHom b) (ModuleCat.ofHom c) (ModuleCat.ofHom b') → ∃! e : PushoutQuotient a b ≃ₗ[R] Q'', e.toLinearMap.comp (pushoutQuotientInl a b) = b' ∧ e.toLinearMap.comp (pushoutQuotientInr a b) = c)
